target_statement: Let p be an odd prime and G a finite p-group of exponent exactly p^2. If the set P={g^p : g in G} of p-th powers is a subgroup of G, then P is abelian.

source_clauses.text: If the p-th powers in a finite p-group form a subgroup, must that subgroup be powerful?
For p not equal to 2, if the p-th powers in a p-group of exponent p^2 form a subgroup, must that subgroup be abelian?
For a 2-group of exponent 8, if the squares form a subgroup, must that subgroup be abelian?

constraints.statement: The assertion quantifies over every prime p and group G satisfying all remaining admissibility rows.
p is prime and p is not 2; equivalently p>2.
G is a finite p-group for that same odd prime p.
The exponent of G is exactly p^2.
P is the set of all actual p-th powers {g^p : g in G}, not merely the subgroup generated by those powers.
The set P of actual p-th powers is closed as a subgroup of G.

excluded_scopes: Any odd-prime group whose exponent is not exactly p^2

success_criteria.proof: Prove P abelian for every odd prime p and every finite p-group G of exponent exactly p^2 whose actual p-th-power set P is a subgroup.
success_criteria.counterexample: Give a reconstructible finite p-group for an explicitly odd prime p, of exponent exactly p^2, whose actual p-th-power set is a subgroup but is nonabelian.
partial_progress: A proved reduction from closure of the p-th-power set to explicit commutator identities.
A complete, reproducible exclusion or construction result for a structurally defined family at an odd prime.
success_criteria.certificate: A line-by-line proof, or a presentation and independent checks of p>2, exact exponent p^2, equality with the actual power set, subgroup closure, and nonabelianity.
